sources.fact: LBBD38/AA Barking Riverside is 179.37ha, deliverable=yes, permissioned, with 10,800 minimum and 20,000 maximum net dwellings; the record notes the 10,800-home outline permission and a pending application to raise housing numbers.
The current Brownfield record supplies a point but blank geometry; that point is not used as an application red-line or HMLR title polygon.
Barking Riverside was originally granted outline permission 04/01230/OUT in 2007 and subsequently varied through 08/00887/FUL.
16/00131/OUT was a further variation application connected to the implemented Barking Riverside permission.
By July 2016, 734 homes had been built in Stage 1 and another 414 were under construction; this is historic delivery evidence, not a current completion count.
The planning committee record describes the Barking Riverside application site as approximately 179.3 hectares.
Regulation 19 materials separately identify AA Barking Riverside as a site-allocation evidence document; allocation provenance is distinct from individual planning permissions.
Current planning status must be verified against exact applications and decisions; no current 20,000-home decision is inferred from the Brownfield maximum.
The Barking Riverside ward has a separate statistical boundary; it is not substituted for the development red-line or parcel title geometry.
Barking Riverside Pier is current transport-access context and does not define the development site or title boundary.
The Brownfield entry contains multiple planning-history links, reinforcing that the masterplan is a multi-application programme rather than one synthetic current consent.
not-owned-by-a-public-authority is an ownership category only and is not converted into a named proprietor or HMLR title.

examples.result: 10,800 is the established outline-permission baseline recorded for AA; 20,000 is a Brownfield maximum and is not treated as already consented.
The pending increase application is not converted into an approval.
Historic 734-built plus 414-under-construction figures are not presented as current 2026 completion totals.
The ward polygon and development point are not used as the Barking Riverside planning red-line.
Transport nodes and pier evidence are context only.
Multiple planning-history records remain separate rather than merged into one synthetic permission.
Ownership category is not converted to legal owner/title evidence.
Promotion remains zero until exact canonical parcel/title relation and current executed statutory overlays are verified.
